LESSON: DIVISION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.3: Division

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Division. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. divide up to a 4-digit number by up to a 3-digit number where the dividend is greater than the divisor in real-life situations
2. estimate quotients by rounding off the dividend and divisor to the nearest ten in real-life situations
3. perform combined operations involving addition, subtraction, multiplication and division up to 3-digit number
4. appreciate use of division of whole numbers in real life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT DIVISION MEANS
Division shares a total into equal groups. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 means 12 split into 3 equal groups of 4.

WORKED EXAMPLES
A: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 because 6 × 4 = 24.
B: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 because 4 × 9 = 36.
C: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 because 5 × 9 = 45.

Check every division by multiplying back.
Real life: 30 exercise books shared equally among 5 learners → 30 ÷ 5 = 6 each.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 (check: 6 × 4 = 24).

Example 2: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 (check: 4 × 9 = 36).

Example 3: Share 30 books among 5 learners → 6 each.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Work out: 18 ÷ 3, 28 ÷ 7, 40 ÷ 8. Multiply back to check.
2. Word problem: 24 oranges shared equally among 6 children. How many each?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Division in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. divide up to a 4-digit number by up to a 3-digit number where the dividend is greater than the divisor in real-life situations
2. estimate quotients by rounding off the dividend and divisor to the nearest ten in real-life situations
3. perform combined operations involving addition, subtraction, multiplication and division up to 3-digit number
4. appreciate use of division of whole numbers in real life

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
